day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Amsterdam Centraal train from Schiphol Airport (€5.40 single, ~17 min). Check in to Canal House Amsterdam and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a self-guided walk along the Herengracht and Prinsengracht canals near the hotel. Explore the Jordaan neighbourhood — one of Amsterdam's most charming districts with free street art, boutique windows, and iconic bridge views. Stop at the Westerkerk church exterior (free to view outside).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to Leidseplein square to soak up the lively atmosphere. Browse the Albert Heijn supermarket on Koningsplein for affordable snacks and drinks to keep costs down tonight.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or sandwich at Schiphol Airport before landing — budget €5–8.
meals.lunch: Broodje Bert or a local bakery near Centraal Station for a fresh Dutch broodje (sandwich) — budget €4–6.
meals.dinner: Dampkring Café area or Foodhallen food market on the edge of Jordaan — try a Dutch bitterballen snack plate and a local beer for around €12–15.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light due to afternoon arrival. Use the evening to orient yourself around the canal belt. Buy an OV-chipkaart (public transport card) at Centraal Station for €7.50 deposit — it will save money all week on trams and buses.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Open from 09:00. Book tickets online in advance to save time (€22.50 per person). Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's masterpieces, and Dutch Golden Age history. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Van Gogh Museum Experience — book timed entry online (€22 per person). Spend 1.5–2 hours discovering The Bedroom, Sunflowers, and the world's largest Van Gogh collection. Afterward, relax in the free Vondelpark just steps away — bring a picnic snack.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the canal belt. Walk along Keizersgracht at dusk when the canal lights begin to reflect on the water — one of Amsterdam's most magical free experiences.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh stroopwafels and coffee at a local bakery near the hotel — budget €4–6.
meals.lunch: Museumplein area — pick up a herring (haring) from a street cart near the museums, a true Dutch budget staple at €3–4, plus a snack from Albert Heijn.
meals.dinner: Wok to Walk on Leidestraat for a filling Asian noodle box — budget €8–10. Eat canal-side for atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Book both the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum tickets online at least 2–3 days ahead — they sell out fast, especially on weekends. Combined museum spend today: ~€44.50 per person but these are the two unmissable highlights of Amsterdam.

day_by_day.morning: Anne Frank House Tour — Book the first available timed slot (09:00 or 09:30 strongly recommended — tickets MUST be pre-booked online, €16 per person). Walk through the hidden annex on Prinsengracht, a deeply moving and historically essential experience. Allow 1.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Anne Frank House, explore the free Amsterdam City Archive (Stadsarchief) on Vijzelstraat — impressive free Art Deco interior and rotating historical exhibitions. Then walk the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) — a charming grid of free-to-browse vintage shops, independent boutiques, and canal crossings between Herengracht and Prinsengracht.
day_by_day.evening: Take Tram 2 or 12 to the NDSM Wharf (free ferry from behind Centraal Station) for a free street art and industrial culture experience along the IJ waterfront. Return by free ferry and walk along Damrak for evening canal views.

meals.breakfast: Café Winkel 43 in Jordaan (famous apple pie) — coffee and a slice for €6–8, right near the Anne Frank House.
meals.lunch: Grab a broodje from Broodje Mokum near the Spui square — budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: Surinamese food at one of the affordable Surinamese-Dutch restaurants near Nieuwmarkt (e.g., Warung Spang Makandra) — hearty rice and roti dishes for €9–12.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House tickets are the most critical booking of the entire trip — they regularly sell out weeks in advance. Book the moment you confirm your travel dates. The NDSM ferry is completely free and offers a different, grittier side of Amsterdam away from tourist crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Private Canal Boat Tour — Book a shared or small-group guided canal boat tour (budget option ~€15–20 per person for a 1-hour group tour vs. private which costs more; opt for a group tour to stay budget-conscious). Cruise the UNESCO-listed canal ring, pass 17th-century merchant houses, and learn the history of Amsterdam's waterways. Depart from near Centraal Station or Leidseplein.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Amsterdam Museum aan de Amstel (Hermitage Amsterdam building) or explore the free Begijnhof — a hidden medieval courtyard garden tucked off Spui, one of Amsterdam's best-kept free secrets. Then walk to the Bloemenmarkt (flower market) on Singel canal — free to browse, iconic tulip bulbs and Dutch souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Red Light District (De Wallen) as a cultural and architectural experience — the medieval Old Church (Oude Kerk) exterior is stunning and the neighbourhood's history is fascinating. Walk Zeedijk street for evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Pick up fresh bread, cheese, and juice from the Albert Heijn near the hotel for a self-catered canal-side breakfast — budget €4–5.
meals.lunch: Vlaams Friteshuis Vleminckx on Voetboogstraat — legendary Amsterdam fries (patat) with your choice of sauce for €3–4. A true local institution.
meals.dinner: Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table) is a Dutch-Indonesian tradition — find a budget version at Kantjil & de Tijger on Spuistraat for a set menu around €18–22, worth a slight splurge for a cultural dining experience.

day_by_day.notes: For the canal boat, compare prices at the docks near Centraal Station — many operators offer walk-up group tours at €15–18 which are far more budget-friendly than private tours. The Begijnhof is completely free and takes only 20–30 minutes but is genuinely magical — do not skip it.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the free EYE Film Museum on the north bank of the IJ (take the free ferry from behind Centraal Station — 5 minutes). The building's architecture alone is worth the trip. Free to enter the ground floor exhibitions and enjoy panoramic views of the Amsterdam skyline across the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city centre and visit the Nieuwmarkt and Jewish Quarter area. Walk to the free exterior of the Portuguese Synagogue (Esnoga) — one of Europe's most beautiful 17th-century synagogues. Browse the Waterlooplein flea market (free entry, open Mon–Sat) for vintage finds and Dutch souvenirs at low prices.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening — return to the Herengracht or Keizersgracht near the hotel for a golden-hour canal walk. Treat yourself to a final Dutch beer at a traditional brown café (bruine kroeg) such as Café 't Smalle in Jordaan — a perfect, atmospheric send-off.

meals.breakfast: Café Bern near Nieuwmarkt for Dutch pancakes (pannenkoeken) — budget €7–9 for a filling start.
meals.lunch: Street food at Waterlooplein market or a quick falafel wrap from one of the budget spots on Reguliersbreestraat — budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: De Foodhallen indoor food market on Bellamyplein — wide variety of international street food stalls, budget €12–16 for a satisfying final meal with great atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and store luggage at the hotel if your flight is in the evening. Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol Airport: take the direct Intercity train (€5.40, every 10–15 minutes, 17 minutes journey). Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for check-in and security. Total estimated 5-day budget per person (excluding flights): accommodation + €95–110 on activities + €80–100 on food = approximately €175–210 on experiences and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Amsterdam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00, so no morning activity. Take the Amsterdam Airport Express (Sprinter) from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal (~17 min, €5.40). Check in at Canal House Amsterdam, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals near the hotel to soak in the atmosphere. Explore the nearby Negen Straatjes (Nine Streets) boutique district for a gentle, low-key introduction to Amsterdam's canal ring and local character.
day_by_day.evening: Private Canal Boat Tour — Book an early-evening departure (typically 17:00–19:00 slots available) to cruise Amsterdam's UNESCO-listed canal ring at golden hour. Glide beneath 17th-century merchant houses and historic bridges with a knowledgeable guide. (~90 minutes, approx. €35–55 per person)

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and stroopwafel at Schiphol airport before landing — no breakfast needed at destination.
meals.lunch: Café Papeneiland near the Jordaan (classic Dutch brown café) — try a broodje kroket (croquette sandwich) and a local beer for ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Greetje (Peperstraat) — a beloved mid-range Dutch restaurant serving traditional Netherlands cuisine with seasonal ingredients. Expect to spend ~€35–45 per person for a two-course meal with a glass of wine.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the afternoon arrival. Pre-book the Canal Boat Tour in advance as evening slots fill quickly in May. Store luggage at Schiphol if needed before check-in time (typically 15:00). Carry an OV-chipkaart or buy a GVB multi-day transit pass upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — Start at 10:00 at the famous Noordermarkt Sunday organic market (open until 15:00). Sample local cheeses, fresh stroopwafels, herring, and artisan goods. Wander the charming Jordaan streets with a guided or self-guided food and culture walk through one of Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhoods. (~2–3 hours, guided tours ~€25–35 per person)
day_by_day.afternoon: Anne Frank House Tour — Walk a short distance to Prinsengracht 263 for your pre-booked time slot (strongly recommended to book 2–3 months ahead). Spend 60–90 minutes walking through the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family hid during WWII. A deeply moving and unmissable experience. (~€16 per person)
day_by_day.evening: Explore Leidseplein square — Amsterdam's lively cultural hub. Catch a performance at the Stadsschouwburg theater or simply enjoy the vibrant street atmosphere with buskers and terrace cafés.

meals.breakfast: Bakker Bart or Café Winkel 43 on Noordermarkt — famous for their apple pie (appeltaart). Coffee and a slice for ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Pick up fresh market food at Noordermarkt — artisan bread, local cheese, and smoked fish for a picnic along the canal for ~€10–15.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Blauw (Amstelveenseweg) — excellent Indonesian rijsttafel (rice table), a Dutch-Indonesian colonial tradition. Mid-range at ~€28–38 per person. Alternatively, try Café de Reiger in the Jordaan for Dutch bistro fare at similar prices.

day_by_day.notes: The Anne Frank House MUST be booked well in advance online — walk-in tickets are rarely available and sell out months ahead, especially on weekends in May. Noordermarkt Sunday market runs 10:00–15:00. Wear comfortable walking shoes as the Jordaan cobblestones can be uneven.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Open from 09:00. Arrive early to beat crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Netherlands' premier art and history museum, home to Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and thousands of Dutch Golden Age masterpieces. The building itself is architecturally stunning. (~€22.50 per person; book tickets online to skip the queue)
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — A short 5-minute walk from the Rijksmuseum in Museumplein. Discover the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works, including 'The Bedroom,' 'Sunflowers,' and 'Wheatfield with Crows.' Allow 1.5–2 hours. (~€22 per person; timed entry tickets must be booked online in advance)
day_by_day.evening: Museumplein and Vondelpark wind-down — After a full museum day, relax in the nearby Vondelpark (Amsterdam's beloved green lung). If energy allows, head to the De Pijp neighborhood for the vibrant Albert Cuypmarkt area and evening drinks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or nearby Lot Sixty One Coffee Roasters (Kinkerstraat) — specialty coffee and pastries for ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Rijksmuseum's own café or the outdoor terrace at Museumplein — sandwiches and soups for ~€12–18. Alternatively, grab a fresh herring (haring) from a street cart for an authentic Dutch snack (~€4).
meals.dinner: Brouwerij 't IJ (the windmill brewery in De Pijp area) for craft beers, then dinner at Café Brecht or Butcher's Tears tap room. Alternatively, try Firma Pekelhaaring in De Pijp for a relaxed mid-range dinner (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is the most museum-intensive day — pace yourself and take breaks. Both the Rijksmuseum and Van Gogh Museum require advance online ticket purchases; same-day availability is extremely limited in May. Consider the Museumkaart (€69.90) if planning to visit more than 3 museums during the trip — it pays for itself quickly. Museumplein is about a 20-minute walk or short tram ride (Tram 2 or 12) from the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Amsterdam's Eastern Canal Ring and Amstel River — Walk or cycle along the Amstel River and the Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge), one of Amsterdam's most photographed drawbridges. Visit the Hermitage-turned-Amstelhof area and the charming Utrechtsestraat shopping street. Rent a bike from MacBike or Starbikes (~€12–15/day) for the most authentic Amsterdam experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: FOAM Photography Museum or Stedelijk Museum (Museum of Modern Art) — For a lighter museum experience after yesterday's intensive day, FOAM on Keizersgracht is intimate, world-class, and rarely overcrowded (~€14). Alternatively, visit the Stedelijk for cutting-edge modern and contemporary art (~€22.50). Both offer a nice contrast to the classical art of Day 3.
day_by_day.evening: Heineken Experience or evening canal-side drinks — Tour the historic Heineken brewery (€23, book online) for a fun, interactive 90-minute experience. Finish the evening with drinks at a classic Amsterdam brown café (bruine kroeg) such as Café 't Smalle or In de Wildeman.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam (if included) or head to Scandinavian Embassy (Sarphatipark) for specialty coffee and smørrebrød open-faced sandwiches (~€10–14).
meals.lunch: Grab a fresh Dutch lunch at Broodje Bert or any local eetcafé along Utrechtsestraat — soup, bread, and a beer for ~€12–16.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Scheepskameel (near Oosterdok) for creative Dutch cuisine in a relaxed setting (~€30–40 per person), or try Brasserie Harkema near Spui for classic French-Dutch brasserie fare at similar prices.

day_by_day.notes: Cycling is highly recommended today — Amsterdam's bike culture is central to the experience and the Eastern Canal Ring is very bike-friendly. Stay alert for tram tracks when cycling. If weather is poor, the afternoon museum visit becomes an even better option. Book Heineken Experience tickets online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip or Neighborhood Discovery — If time allows before departure, take a 20-minute train to Haarlem (€4.50 each way) for a charming, less-touristy Dutch city experience with the Frans Hals Museum and Grote Markt. Alternatively, explore Amsterdam's NDSM Wharf (free ferry from Centraal) for street art and creative culture, or visit the A'DAM Lookout tower for panoramic city views (~€17.50).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping and canal farewell — Browse Waterlooplein Flea Market for vintage finds and unique souvenirs. Walk the Bloemenmarkt (floating flower market) on Singel for Dutch tulip bulbs and Delftware gifts. Enjoy a final leisurely canal-side coffee or jenever (Dutch gin) tasting at a local proeflokaal (tasting house) such as Wynand Fockink near Dam Square.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and departure preparation — Pack up at Canal House Amsterdam and enjoy a final dinner before any late flights or next-day departures. Spend a quiet final evening along the Herengracht, reflecting on the trip.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast or De Bakkerswinkel (Warmoesstraat) — beloved Amsterdam bakery with excellent pastries, quiches, and coffee for ~€10–14.
meals.lunch: If day-tripping to Haarlem: lunch at Grand Café Brinkmann on Grote Markt (~€15–20). If staying in Amsterdam: Café Luxembourg on Spui for a classic Dutch lunch (~€14–18).
meals.dinner: Restaurant d'Vijff Vlieghen (The Five Flies) — a historic Amsterdam institution in five 17th-century canal houses near Spui, serving refined Dutch cuisine. A memorable farewell dinner at ~€40–55 per person. Book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (typically 11:00 — arrange late checkout or luggage storage if needed). Amsterdam Centraal to Schiphol airport takes only 17 minutes by direct train; allow at least 2.5–3 hours before any international flight departure. The Haarlem day trip works best if you have a full day and no early evening commitments. Waterlooplein Market is open Monday–Saturday; confirm it's open on Wednesday before planning around it.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight KL lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Transfer from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol to Canal House Amsterdam via private chauffeur service (pre-arranged luxury transfer, approx. 30–40 min). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your canal-view suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Canal Boat Tour — After settling in, embark on a private guided canal boat cruise departing from a nearby jetty on the Herengracht. Glide beneath 17th-century drawbridges, past the iconic Golden Bend, and through the UNESCO-listed canal ring. Your knowledgeable guide will share stories of Amsterdam's mercantile Golden Age. Duration: approx. 2 hours. Perfect introduction to the city at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll the Jordaan neighborhood at dusk — one of Amsterdam's most atmospheric quarters, just steps from the hotel. Browse boutique galleries and admire the illuminated canal facades before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport lounge on arrival day)
meals.lunch: Light welcome refreshments at Canal House Amsterdam upon check-in, or a quick stop at Café Papeneiland — a historic 17th-century brown café on the Prinsengracht serving Dutch apple pie and artisan sandwiches.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vinkeles — a Michelin-starred restaurant set inside a former bakery of the Dylan Hotel on the Keizersgracht. Expect refined French-Dutch tasting menus with exceptional wine pairings. Reservation essential; book in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer before departure. Request a canal-facing room at Canal House Amsterdam for the full experience. The canal boat tour can be booked through the hotel concierge for a seamless, premium experience. Keep the first afternoon relaxed given travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Rijksmuseum Visit — Begin the day with a private guided tour of the Netherlands' premier art and history museum. Marvel at Rembrandt's 'The Night Watch,' Vermeer's 'The Milkmaid,' and Delftware collections. A private guide (arranged through the hotel concierge) ensures skip-the-line access and an intimate, in-depth experience. Duration: approx. 2.5–3 hours. The museum opens at 09:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Van Gogh Museum Experience — A short walk from the Rijksmuseum, the Van Gogh Museum houses the world's largest collection of Van Gogh's works. Explore 'The Bedroom,' 'Sunflowers,' and his moving self-portraits in roughly chronological order. Pre-booked timed entry is a must. Afterwards, take a leisurely walk through Vondelpark — Amsterdam's elegant green lung — just adjacent to both museums.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to freshen up, then enjoy a sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace or lounge overlooking the canal before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — enjoy a curated in-house breakfast spread with fresh pastries, artisan cheeses, smoked salmon, and freshly squeezed juices in the elegant dining room.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Rijksmuseum's Grand Café Cobra or the museum's refined restaurant — a stylish setting beneath the museum's iconic arched gallery. Alternatively, picnic provisions from a nearby artisan deli enjoyed in Vondelpark.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ciel Bleu — Amsterdam's celebrated two-Michelin-starred restaurant on the 23rd floor of Hotel Okura. Breathtaking panoramic city views paired with an exceptional contemporary European tasting menu and sommelier-led wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Rijksmuseum private guide and Van Gogh Museum timed-entry tickets well in advance — both are extremely popular, especially on Saturdays. Wear comfortable shoes for museum walking. The Museumplein area is walkable from the hotel via a scenic canal route.

day_by_day.morning: Jordaan Neighborhood Food & Culture Walk — Join a premium small-group or private food and culture walking tour through Amsterdam's most picturesque neighborhood. Visit the famous Noordermarkt Sunday organic market (open 09:00–15:00) for local cheeses, stroopwafels, fresh herring, and artisan produce. Explore hidden courtyards (hofjes), independent galleries, and charming boutiques along the Bloemgracht and Egelantiersgracht canals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Anne Frank House Tour — A profoundly moving visit to the hidden annex where Anne Frank and her family concealed themselves during World War II. Premium timed-entry tickets (booked well in advance) allow a reflective, unhurried experience. The museum also features original diary pages and historical context exhibits. Duration: approx. 1.5 hours. The Anne Frank House is located in the heart of the Jordaan, making it a natural continuation of the morning walk.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Nine Streets (De Negen Straatjes) — a charming grid of specialty shops, antique dealers, and concept stores connecting the main canals. Browse at leisure before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Canvas — the rooftop restaurant of the Volkshotel, offering panoramic Amsterdam views and a creative brunch menu. Alternatively, enjoy breakfast at the hotel and walk to the Noordermarkt for market tastings.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Worst Wijncafé in the Jordaan — a beloved neighbourhood wine bar and charcuterie spot offering outstanding Dutch and European cured meats, cheeses, and natural wines in a relaxed setting.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Breda — an acclaimed Amsterdam restaurant on the Singel canal known for its ingredient-driven, seasonal tasting menus and warm, intimate atmosphere. One of Amsterdam's most celebrated fine dining destinations.

day_by_day.notes: Anne Frank House tickets must be booked online months in advance — they sell out extremely quickly, especially on weekends. The Noordermarkt Sunday market is a highlight not to be missed. The Jordaan is best explored on foot; the entire day is concentrated in this walkable, charming district.

day_by_day.morning: Private Morning Canal Kayak or Paddleboard Experience — For an active, intimate perspective on the canals, arrange a private guided kayak or stand-up paddleboard tour through the quieter waterways of the Eastern Canal Ring and Plantage neighborhood. Early morning is magical — calm waters, few tourists, and beautiful golden light on the canal houses. Duration: approx. 2 hours. Alternatively, arrange a second private canal boat tour focused on the lesser-known eastern canals and the Amstel River.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Plantage & Jewish Quarter — Visit the Portuguese Synagogue (Esnoga), one of Europe's most stunning 17th-century synagogues, and the adjacent Jewish Historical Museum. Stroll through the Hortus Botanicus — one of the world's oldest botanical gardens, founded in 1638 — a serene and beautiful afternoon retreat. Finish with a walk along the Amstel River and the iconic Magere Brug (Skinny Bridge).
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa and wellness session — treat yourself to an evening at the Sofitel Legend The Grand Amsterdam's spa, or the Okura Hotel's renowned Nagomi Spa, for a restorative massage or hydrotherapy treatment after days of exploration.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — arrange a private breakfast served in your suite with canal views. A true luxury indulgence.
meals.lunch: Lunch at De Kas — a legendary Amsterdam restaurant set inside a stunning 1926 greenhouse in Frankendael Park. Hyper-seasonal, garden-to-table cuisine where nearly everything is grown on-site. A unique and memorable dining experience.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rijsel — a beloved Amsterdam brasserie in a former school gymnasium, known for its outstanding roast chicken, seasonal vegetables, and convivial atmosphere. A more relaxed but still premium dining experience — a local favourite.

day_by_day.notes: The kayak/paddleboard experience should be booked through a premium operator offering private guiding. De Kas requires a reservation and is worth the short taxi ride to Frankendael Park. The Plantage neighborhood is less touristy and offers a more authentic Amsterdam experience.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in and enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast at the hotel. Take a final solo stroll along the Herengracht and Keizersgracht canals to absorb the beauty of Amsterdam's canal ring at a relaxed pace. Visit a favourite spot or canal-side café for a final Dutch coffee and apple cake. Pick up artisan souvenirs — Delftware, Dutch gin (jenever), or artisan cheese — from specialty shops near the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Amsterdam Museum of the Canals (Grachtenhuis) — a compact but fascinating museum located in a beautifully restored canal house on the Herengracht, dedicated entirely to the history and engineering of Amsterdam's iconic canal system. A perfect, unhurried final cultural experience that ties together the canal theme of the trip. Duration: approx. 1–1.5 hours. Afterwards, return to the hotel for final packing and checkout.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — a celebratory final meal before departure preparations.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury breakfast at Canal House Amsterdam — savour every last moment of the canal views with a full spread of Dutch cheeses, pastries, eggs, and fresh-pressed juice.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Restaurant Amsterdam — a grand, atmospheric brasserie set inside a converted 19th-century pumping house in the Westerpark area, with beautiful Art Nouveau interiors and excellent Dutch-European cuisine.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Spectrum at the Waldorf Astoria Amsterdam — a Michelin-starred gem set within a row of six restored 17th-century canal houses. An extraordinary setting with a world-class tasting menu and impeccable service. The perfect luxurious send-off for a premium Amsterdam trip.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with Canal House Amsterdam and arrange private chauffeur transfer back to Schiphol Airport in advance. The Grachtenhuis museum is an ideal final activity — close to the hotel and thematically perfect for a canal-focused trip. Keep the afternoon light to allow time for packing and a stress-free departure.
